summary: Shasta National Forest summit lookout reported standing in September 1932; the FFLA county list now marks the tower gone, with no removal date.

facts.status_note: FFLA county list marks the tower gone; no removal date or site description in the sources read

events.note: Dunsmuir News report (September 16, 1932, quoted on Forest Lookouts) says one lookout already stands on the summit; the article gives no build date

evidence.supports: two more lookout stations in the Shasta National Forest were being built in 1932 so firefighters could find and suppress blazes faster
evidence.quote: to enable fire fighters more quickly to locate and suppress blazes

evidence.supports: the stations were being constructed that summer
one lookout stands on the summit of Brock Mountain, eight miles east of Bully Hill
evidence.quote: One lookout stands upon the summit of Brock Mountain, eight miles east of Bully Hill.

evidence.supports: the report is from the Dunsmuir News
county Shasta; position 40.80502, -122.13218; tower listed as gone

notes_for_editor: Only two sources: a 1932 newspaper item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page and one county-list row. The statewide FFLA list (firelookout.org/lookouts/us/ca/) prints a 'Standing' status and NHLR US 378, CA 39 in the row region above Brock Mountain, but NHLR US 378 is Breckenridge Lookout in Kern County in our NHLR cache, so the statewide row cells do not line up with the names. Do not use them; the county table (ca-co) reads Tower Gone. No NHLR entry for Brock in the cache. Brief status gone and agency are supported. The 1932 article gives no build date, so 1932 is only the earliest date a lookout is reported on the summit; the story claims no build year. The source does not say whether the summit lookout was one of the two stations under construction that summer, so the story does not link them.
